records.researcher_notes: PJM's first-cycle queue lists request C01-1570: 347 MW of natural gas generation in Ogle County, Illinois, from Ogle County Hub LLC. It was filed on April 25, 2026, connects at the Byron 345 kV switchyard, and asks to be in service by December 31, 2029. I read these values from PJM's own full queue export, downloaded on October 29, 2026. The interconnection.fyi page for the request at https://www.interconnection.fyi/project/pjm-c01-1570 shows the same size, fuel, county, developer and completion date. PJM's page for the request at https://www.pjm.com/m/ProjectTransition/SISReportDetails?queueNumber=C01-1570 confirms the queue number, the developer and the filing date. A grid queue entry makes the status announced. The plant is named after the developer's company name, since no other name is published. The owner is Ogle County Hub LLC at 100 percent. PJM's page for the request names it as the company behind the request, and the interconnection.fyi page says the project is owned by it. Both pages were checked again on October 30, 2026. GEM accepts a project company as the owner. The parent company is Constellation Energy. Two reports Constellation Energy Corporation filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, on April 15 and July 20, 2026, list Ogle County Hub LLC among the companies where its officers hold posts, and the July report says Constellation Energy Corporation owns enough of each listed company to elect its directors. Both reports were checked on October 30, 2026. Constellation Energy is already in GEM's company list as entity 100001000208, so it is not a new company. Ogle County Hub LLC is not in GEM's company list, so it is a new company record. The size and fuel come from a queue tracker site, not PJM's own page, so they are less certain until PJM posts a study report. Not found: a news story, permit, site or turbine type. PJM's full queue file, downloaded October 21, 2026, gives only Natural Gas for request C01-1570, and the interconnection.fyi page gives only Gas, so Technology is unknown. The point is the Byron nuclear station, where the request connects at the Byron 345 kV switchyard, from the EIA monthly generator file for September 2026, plant 6023 on the Operating sheet. It is approximate, the same way Prairie Pulse is placed at the LaSalle station. Checked for duplicates on October 30, 2026. GEM has no plant of any fuel at the Byron nuclear station, where this request connects, and none within 20 kilometers. The watch item for the Byron to Wayne gas request in Lee County is a different request on a different line. No GEM wiki page names Ogle County Hub LLC. Three gas requests of about 346 MW each were filed on the same day at Constellation's Braidwood, Byron and LaSalle nuclear stations, and the same reports tie all three companies to Constellation. They are separate sites, so each is its own plant.

records.researcher_notes: The Tilton Energy Center is an operating 188 MW gas peaking plant at 80 West First Street in Tilton, Vermilion County, Illinois, that is missing from GEM. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists it as plant 7760, Tilton Energy LLC, with four 47 MW natural gas turbines in service since June 1999. The Illinois EPA Clean Air Act permit 00050017, issued April 30, 2019 and revised February 15, 2022, names Tilton Energy, LLC as the source and lists four 47 MW natural gas combustion turbines built in May and June 1999 with water injection. An October 2011 stack test report filed with the Illinois EPA says the four turbines are identical General Electric LM-6000 simple cycle machines. Aeroderivative turbines installed together are one GEM unit, so the four turbines are entered as one unit with four engines of 47 MW each, 188 MW in total. Published totals vary: Dynegy's 2000 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission says 176 MW, Rockland Capital's July 2017 sale release says 180 MW, and POWER Magazine's September 2022 article says 184 MW. The nameplate figure of 47 MW per turbine from the permit and the EIA table is used. History: Illinois Power leased the turbines in 1999 and subleased them to Dynegy Midwest Generation, Dynegy bought them in 2004, Rockland Capital acquired the plant in 2014 or 2015 and sold it in July 2017 to a Carlyle Group fund, and Earthrise Energy bought it from Rockland Capital in February 2022, according to POWER Magazine. The owner is Tilton Energy LLC at 100 percent. It is not in GEM's company list, so it is a new company record. Earthrise Energy is already in GEM's company list as entity 100000002885 and is the parent. The operator is not filled in. The only page naming an operator is the company's own website, which is a lead and not a citation. The location is exact. The EIA-860M point, 40.10612, -87.65382, lands on the four turbine packages beside the switchyard in satellite imagery: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=40.10612,-87.65382. Checked for duplicates on October 30, 2026 against the full GEM export by name, by county and by distance. No GEM plant matches. Not found: a published retirement plan, a current capacity market or interconnection filing, and a document naming the operator.
